question: How is limited knowing itself bondage, and what removes it?
premises: Even impurity is contracted distinct knowing, not a separate thing.
The dualist makes bondage external; Kṣemarāja shows it is mis-knowing sustained by hidden freedom.
The three malas — atomic, māyic, actional — are this contraction at three depths.
inference: Bondage is knowing-as-limited; recognition alone removes it.
uncertainties: Long fused compounds segmented by sense; Pratyabhijñā quotes rendered as cited.
plain_english: Knowing is bondage: even impurity is contracted distinct knowing. The dualist externalizes bondage, but it is mis-knowing — atomic, māyic, and actional malas are one contraction. Thus the sūtra is stated so that recognition removes it.
